WEDE5020 Web Development (Introduction)

Build a campus repair café website, from the first project brief to testing a published page.

Open the WEDE5020 module

Learning units

Unit 1. Introduction to web development

Decide what a campus repair café needs from its website and how the team will know whether it helps visitors.

  • Choose an online presence
  • Measure visitor and organisation goals
  • How HTML, CSS and JavaScript work together
  • Source, credit and optimise assets

Unit 2. Website files and Visual Studio Code

Set up the project folder and trace the paths a browser uses to find its pages, images and styles.

  • Organise folders and follow relative paths
  • Create and preview a project in VS Code

Unit 3. Introduction to HTML

Build a linked, semantic website and verify that text, media and forms have a sensible reading order.

  • Read HTML syntax and the document tree
  • Use semantic elements, media, tables and forms
  • Build linked pages and validate the HTML

Unit 4. Styling websites with CSS

Give the café pages a consistent visual style and explain why a particular CSS declaration wins.

  • Link a stylesheet and trace the cascade
  • Style boxes, type, links and layout
  • Debug a shared stylesheet with DevTools

Unit 5. Responsive web design

Keep the timetable and enquiry link usable from a narrow phone to a wide desktop.

  • Build a mobile-first layout and test breakpoints

Unit 6. Building functionality into websites

Add a small JavaScript enhancement and choose how to collect a visitor’s response.

  • Use JavaScript and jQuery for page behaviour
  • Validate forms, embed Google Forms and collect responses

Unit 7. SEO, publishing and maintenance

Publish a discoverable website, test its public pages and use evidence to decide what to improve.

  • Help visitors and search engines find a page
  • Choose a domain, publish and test a website
  • Interpret analytics and maintain the site
